daily_brief: Sunday's global news landscape is dominated by pivotal events across multiple continents. In Brazil, nearly 160 million voters are casting ballots in a high-stakes presidential election pitting incumbent Lula da Silva against Flavio Bolsonaro, with regional implications tied to the broader rightward shift in Latin America [France 24, Le Monde]. Meanwhile, Russia intensified its campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, striking major Kyiv bridges for the fourth consecutive day as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to demonstrate European solidarity [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. Tensions between Iran and the United States remain elevated, with Tehran declaring the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until its seven conditions are met, while Foreign Minister Araghchi insisted there is no military solution to the conflict [The Hindu]. In France, allegations of antisemitic comments made by far-right leader Jordan Bardella as a teenager have thrown the National Rally into crisis weeks before crucial elections [RFI]. Across Spain, tens of thousands protested a deepening housing crisis after the government's emergency legislation failed in Congress, raising the prospect of early elections [BBC]. These developments underscore persistent geopolitical friction, democratic stress-testing, and social unrest shaping the current international order.

top_stories.headline: Brazil Votes in Tight Presidential Election Between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
bullets: Nearly 160 million Brazilians began voting Sunday in a presidential election pitting 80-year-old incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against 45-year-old Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
If no candidate receives more than 50% of the vote, a runoff will be held on October 25; voters are also electing lawmakers, senators, and governors.
The election reflects a regional contest between Lula's closer ties with Beijing and Bolsonaro's alignment with U.S. President Donald Trump, amid a broader rightward shift in Latin American politics.
Concerns over potential U.S. interference and a lackluster campaign have marked the election period.

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasizes the Trump-Bolsonaro alliance and regional ideological context.

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Highlights concerns over U.S. interference and describes the campaign as lackluster.

top_stories.headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridges for Fourth Day as German Chancellor Merz Visits Ukraine
bullets: Russian drone strikes hit major bridges in Kyiv for the fourth consecutive day, injuring two people and damaging the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge on Sunday.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made an unannounced visit to Kyiv, meeting with President Zelensky to reaffirm support and warn that Russia's war machine could eventually target Europe.
Russia's military announced it would intensify strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, claiming the bridges were used for military transport.
President Zelensky said Ukraine would respond by doubling down on attacks against Russian oil refineries, citing intelligence about a new Russian doctrine targeting civilian infrastructure.

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Detailed tactical reporting on bridge strikes and verified video footage.

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief report focused on the timing of the Merz visit.

sources.name: Le Monde

top_stories.headline: Iran Demands Seven Conditions Met Before Reopening Strait of Hormuz
bullets: Iran's Parliament Speaker declared the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions outlined in a June interim agreement with the U.S. are fulfilled.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated there is no military solution to the conflict and called for negotiations based on 'justice and fairness.'

The U.S. and Iran held indirect talks at the UN General Assembly last week, but President Trump rejected Iran's proposal while leaving the door open to further discussions or renewed military operations.
Iran has sought to control the vital shipping lane since the start of hostilities, attacking vessels that transit without authorization.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Detailed reporting on Iranian diplomatic positions and Qalibaf's statements via Nournews.

top_stories.headline: Antisemitism Allegations Threaten Political Future of French Far-Right Leader Jordan Bardella
bullets: French investigative outlet Mediapart published allegations and screenshots of antisemitic comments allegedly made by National Rally leader Jordan Bardella on Facebook Messenger in 2013.
Bardella, 31, denied the allegations, calling them fabrications and vowing to take Mediapart to court.
Marine Le Pen initially defended Bardella but fell largely silent after screenshots were published Thursday, saying only that she has 'complete confidence' in him.
The scandal threatens to derail the National Rally's momentum heading into presidential elections in which Le Pen is polling favorably.

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive account of the allegations, Bardella's response, and Le Pen's reaction.

top_stories.headline: Tens of Thousands Protest Housing Crisis Across Spain After Government Legislation Fails
bullets: Approximately 50 marches took place across Spain on Saturday, including in Madrid, Valencia, and Barcelona, with tens of thousands demanding tenant protections and an end to evictions.

The protests were sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman unable to afford a sharp rent increase, and intensified after the Sánchez government's emergency housing legislation failed in Congress on Friday.
Clashes occurred between protesters and police in Valencia near a real estate summit.
The legislative defeat raises speculation that Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez may call early elections; his coalition lacks a parliamentary majority.

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Neutral account focusing on protest scale and political implications.
